assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, insulinotropic action) translated into long-acting agonists that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Importance, clinical scale and lasting impact are exceptional, and the physiology-to-medicine arc fits the prize well.
assessment.attribution: Holst (characterization of the active truncated GLP-1 and its physiology), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, receptor and therapeutic concepts) and Knudsen (design of liraglutide/semaglutide) cover discovery, physiology and drug development. Mojsov's peptide-chemistry contribution is credited but a three-person cap forces a hard choice; other early contributors outside the supplied credit are not assessable.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent confirmations, large outcome trials and widespread clinical use; recognition is timely, with the field still expanding.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Drucker, Holst and others is contested and I cannot independently verify priority details.
Knudsen is an industry scientist; the committee may prefer a purely discovery-based trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, a conserved ER-to-nucleus signaling pathway (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing), is a foundational cell-biological concept with broad relevance to secretory disease, neurodegeneration and cancer. Clear, original and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the central figures: Mori for UPR element and transcriptional response in yeast and mammals, Walter for IRE1 as the sensor and the mechanism of signal transduction. Both are named, giving a clean configuration; other contributors to the pathway (e.g., Ron, Kaufman) lie outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation across species; mechanism well established and recognition is mature, if arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the mammalian branches (PERK, ATF6) beyond the supplied names may be raised.
Direct clinical translation is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality. Strong clinical impact and a clear conceptual advance in engineering immunity.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed the early chimeric receptor and costimulation design concepts; June led pivotal clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T. Rosenberg is credited for adoptive cell therapy and early clinical CAR work, but his core contribution (TIL therapy) is a partly distinct discovery, so I would favour two laureates.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent clinical confirmation; long-term data, toxicity management and solid-tumour extension remain in progress, but recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among Eshhar, Sadelain, June, Rosenberg and others is disputed; I have not verified details.
Compound discovery: design concept versus clinical translation may call for different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics enabled causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity with light, transforming neuroscience and experimental physiology. Highly original, widely adopted tool with lasting methodological impact.
assessment.attribution: Credit is genuinely difficult: six credited names. Miesenböck (first genetically targeted photoactivation concept), Hegemann/Bamberg/Nagel (channelrhodopsin characterization) and Deisseroth/Boyden (neuronal deployment). I propose Deisseroth, Miesenböck and Hegemann as a plausible but imperfect trio, leaving out Nagel, Bamberg and Boyden.
assessment.maturity: Technology has been confirmed in thousands of laboratories for over fifteen years; clinical application is emerging (vision restoration), so maturity is high for the tool itself.
uncertainties: The three-person limit excludes equally credible contributors; attribution is the main obstacle.
The prize emphasises a tool; the committee may weigh discovery against technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection, precancer and cervical cancer, with population-level effectiveness data showing sharp declines in disease. A major preventive medicine achievement.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (VLP development with Zhou, who is deceased) form the usual configuration. Independent parallel work by other groups (e.g., Georgetown/Rochester/Merck and GSK developments) may complicate fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Strong population-level confirmation across countries; recognition is timely to somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Priority among groups developing L1 VLPs is disputed and I cannot verify details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and the central nutrient- and growth-signaling kinase revealed how cells coordinate growth with environment, with implications in cancer, metabolism, immunity and ageing.
assessment.attribution: Hall's discovery of TOR in yeast and demonstration of its role in growth control is the decisive contribution. Schreiber (FKBP12-rapamycin chemical biology) and Sabatini (mTOR/mTORC1 in mammals) were important, but a Hall-led single or limited configuration is cleaner; I propose Hall alone while noting Sabatini's contributions are intertwined with other considerations.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and expanded by many groups; therapeutic uses of rapalogs exist, though full clinical impact of pathway targeting is incomplete.
uncertainties: Fair inclusion of Schreiber and Sabatini versus other mTOR contributors is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids, built on Lgr5 stem-cell identification and long-term culture, created a broadly used platform for tissue biology, disease modelling and personalised medicine.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear intellectual leader (Lgr5 and organoid culture); Sato executed the pioneering intestinal organoid culture work. A two-person configuration is supported by the supplied credit; other organoid pioneers fall outside the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently reproduced; clinical and translational impact is still maturing, so recognition is plausible but possibly early.
uncertainties: Relative importance of the Lgr5 discovery versus the organoid method is not fully clear.
Competing organoid lineages (pluripotent-stem-cell derived) may complicate scope.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cGAS as the cytosolic DNA sensor producing cGAMP and activating STING defined a core innate-immune pathway with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunotherapy and ageing. Elegant and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger; Barber identified STING. Other credited names (Ishikawa, Wu, Sun) were closely involved, but a two-laureate prize of Chen and Barber best reflects the decisive findings. Contributions of other groups (e.g., Vance, Patel, Hornung) lie outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and extensively; therapeutic translation is early, and some timing argues for waiting.
uncertainties: Clinical translation is not yet established.
Priority and the fair role of trainees and competing groups cannot be verified by me.
